changes.subject: paper-v4/experiment-v4/run-19/bind_from_surface.py
changes.detail: The evaluator writes one file of type sets per question, read from the accepted population surface at ontology acceptance and before phase two exists. bind_from_surface.py expands it deterministically into the exhaustive binding: every ordered pair of a question's types under every relation type on the surface, with a fixed field projection per type made of that type's non-housekeeping slots, carrying bound_at_stage ONTOLOGY_ACCEPTANCE. Its digest is recorded in the launch log at acceptance and the query runs it unchanged after replay; only bound_after_replay_receipt_sha256 moves from PENDING to the receipt digest, and cases_sha256 digests the queries alone so the executed binding is provably the one the launch log pinned. The producer never sees any of it.
changes.why: Deep sweep D-01. Run-04's own binding records in bound_by that a hand-picked draft returned no row for CQ-03 and was replaced, and that a second draft's CQ-04 type set was cut once its 75 citation rows were visible. No value or identifier entered the binding, but the selection between bindings was conditioned on the result, which the manuscript's binding rule and the master plan's submission gate both exclude in kind.

changes.subject: src/malleus/_contract_pipeline/document.py
changes.detail: Three checks over the derivation rule's content rather than its existence. A DIGEST_MISMATCH refusal in the document adapter when a record's assertion_locator names an assertion of the same capture and its statement_sha256 is not that assertion's statement digest, aggregated. Modality-disposition consistency: a field a pack marks evaluative must be formalized by at least one assertion whose modality is not HYPOTHESISED, aggregated. Derivation-locality and fan-out as census axes: per relation, whether the formalizing assertion's block is among the blocks that formalize an endpoint, and per assertion, how many distinct records it formalizes, both reported beside the census and neither refused. The pin script fills the reason names from the diagnostic enum at the pinned commit; nothing here names a reason Core has not landed. The adapter takes the compiled contract view as an optional argument (None for older runners); run-09's run.py passes retention.contract_view so the evaluative-slot check is in force, and test_pipeline.py pins that one-line difference from run-04's runner. Carried into v4.3 unchanged. Its reasons are read between its own baseline and the v4.2 coordinate, both fixed commits, so a reason Core-13 adds cannot be attributed to Core-12; the pin only records whether the three are still in force at the v4.3 coordinate.
changes.why: handover/2026-09-05-run-04-review-rca.md. All 104 of run-04's located claims carried a correct statement digest and nothing recomputed one; one assertion carried thirty-six formalization targets for twelve relations it names no endpoint of; all five hypothesis dispositions derive from the sentence that states the hypothesis, never from the sentence that disposes of it. The protocol proved a pointer existed and left what it pointed at to review.

The pin script fills what the pinned commit carries: every refusal reason the enum gained after the v4.3 coordinate, the elaborator's INVALID_RANGE message text verbatim beside the v4.3 coordinate's, whether it moved, and whether a bound scalar range is named literally in it, and the skill's digest beside the v4.3 coordinate's. changes.why: handover/2026-09-05-v43-rca.md sections 6, 7 and 8, and E-0143. Twenty of run-09's 212 source-asserted records carry an assertion_modality that no formalizing assertion carries, MEASURED in the capture against STATED on the record twelve times; run-04 and run-08 had zero. The record's modality is a copy of the assertion's, set by the producer a second time, and this cell's producer tagged the clause where the capture tagged the sentence. The reviewers judged all twenty on the prose and flagged them, which is a check the protocol should be making. The two ride-alongs are the two returns that recurred: both Opus cells on the current skill spent their first ontology attempt on a date or uri range, and run-09 spent its first runner attempt on names. Neither is a rule gap; both are the protocol not stating what it already checks.

changes.detail: The name-or-tag comparison becomes word-bounded at both sites that make it: the SUBJECT_NOT_NAMED check and the subject census. A form occurs in a statement when its non-whitespace characters appear in order with any whitespace between them, case-insensitively, and the match is adjacent to no letter on either side; digits and punctuation are boundaries, so the text layer's glued citation digits still name and an occurrence inside another word does not. One predicate serves both sites and replaces the whitespace-free substring test Core-15 widened the check to. The rule does not change: a source-asserted record's subject is the one the producer set or none, and the subject entity's name or one of its tags must occur in a statement that formalizes the record. What changes is what counts as occurring. No refusal reason is added and none is removed, so expected_reasons is empty and the enum cannot report the change; SUBJECT_NOT_NAMED's condition is narrowed, so a subject matched only inside another word is now refused and an inflected or glued form costs the producer a tag. The census keeps Core-17's four outcomes and counts them under the same predicate, which is why attachable and ambiguous fall. subject is the slot Core-13 added and tags an existing root slot, so there is no new slot, no pack version and no ontology change. One skill sentence says a name occurs as a word. The pin reads the adapter at the pinned commit, resolves both sites by AST, and records for each whether it calls the shared bounded predicate and whether a substring test against a statement is still in it; pin_status is LANDED only when both sites carry the predicate, neither carries the substring test, and the adapter and the skill have both moved off the v4.7 coordinate. Carried into v4.9 unchanged: this entry states what v4.8 landed, not what v4.9 expects. This cell pins the same Core coordinate as run-14, so the two byte comparisons, the enum difference and the census outcome keys are read between the v4.7 coordinate 12a04a9 and the v4.8 coordinate dc52547, which are fixed commits. The pin still resolves both subject sites by AST at the pinned commit and refuses outright if the shared predicate is gone or a membership test against a statement is back, because a carried entry that read LANDED without reading the adapter would be a claim about bytes nobody opened.
changes.why: handover/2026-09-05-overseer-journal.md, iteration 5 RCA before the review, decision 23, and E-0160. Run-13's 33 attachable records were read one by one against the entity each names: 14 name a tool, model or instrument, and the tag LAB was found sitting inside "available". Measured by script over the retained captures of runs 11 to 13, eight of run-12's fifteen projected subjects were in-word matches of three-letter tags: RTI in "vertical" and "portion", OCC in "occur", MAR in "mark", OBS in "observations". E-0155 and E-0157 read those thirteen subjects as wrong and attributed them to a sentence naming its instrument as often as its subject; the subjects are wrong as read and the attribution is not, which E-0160 corrects. Of the seven matched as a word, three attach a record to its software, one is marginal and three are plausible, so the attribution rests on three or four cases and not on thirteen. The comparison strips whitespace and tests substring; it has no word boundary, and the check has been reading in-word matches as names since Core-15. This is the loop's third clarification of an existing check, after ranges and names and after tags, and the three keep finding the same thing: the rule was right and the comparison was loose.

changes.subject: src/malleus/_contract_pipeline/document.py
changes.detail: Four fixes to what the protocol reports, none to what it admits. The block census labels every block of the reading ASSERTED, DECLARED_NOTHING_ASSERTABLE or UNTOUCHED and counts the three, keeping blocks_reviewed as the sum of the first two with its meaning stated. A provenance axis reports, per type that carries assertion_locator, how many records reach the assertion behind them and how many bind its bytes. The rehydration failure that reached run-17's runner as a raw ValueError is typed RECORDS_NOT_REHYDRATABLE in the plan compiler's enum. GAP_REQUIRED runs as a pre-pass that collects every assertion with neither a formalization target nor a gap and refuses once, instead of naming the first.
changes.why: Run-16 and run-17 both left the record saying something that is not true. Run-16's census counted 186 of 186 blocks reviewed when 128 of them were a producer claim the census cannot check; run-17's counted 186 when the capture named seven. The two protocol observations of E-0176 are the other half: the paper claims every refusal is typed, and at the rehydration stage that was false, and GAP_REQUIRED spent a return on one assertion when eight were in the same state. This cell reads the fixes because its producer is the one that met all four.
changes.expected_reasons_basis: One reason is typed where the graph gate's exception passed through untyped, and none is removed. The pin computes the difference of the plan compiler's enum between the v4.9 coordinate and the pinned commit and compares it to this list; the document adapter's enum is expected to be unchanged and the pin records that difference too.
changes.aggregation_non_evidence: The document adapter's enum carries GAP_REQUIRED at both coordinates, so the enum difference cannot report the aggregation. What the AST can see is _empty_assertion_defects, which collects every empty assertion, and _refuse_gaps, which renders them as one refusal, both module-level functions and neither present at the v4.9 coordinate. That is what this entry records and it is recorded as what it is.
changes.pin_evidence: The pin resolves the three block labels inside _block_census by AST and records every label-shaped constant it finds, so a fourth label is reported rather than hidden; it records whether the adapter writes provenance_coverage as a literal; it computes the plan compiler's enum difference between the two coordinates; and it resolves the two GAP_REQUIRED functions by name. LANDED requires all six observations, and the adapter and the plan compiler both moved since the v4.9 coordinate.
changes.producer_visible_note: Visible only through the skill, which Core-20 moves. Core-19 changes no rule the producer must follow; it changes what the census says about what the producer did, and it types one refusal the producer already met untyped.
changes.carried_note: Run-18's entry, carried. This cell pins the commit run-18 pinned, so the pin reads it again there against the same v4.8 baseline rather than copying run-18's status: pin_status is recomputed from the bytes and must come back LANDED.

changes.subject: .claude/skills/malleus-acolyte/SKILL.md
changes.governance_note: The pin decides pin_status on the bytes at the pinned commit and records the governance head beside it. Core-20's code may be at the commit this cell pins before its overseer entry is written, and this cell may be pinned in that state; governance_entry_landed says which, and the overseer re-pins after the entry lands.
changes.detail: The skill gains one paragraph between two markers: the adapter's and the plan compiler's refusal reasons as the producer's pre-flight, one line per reason with the check in plain words. A guard in tests/test_inquisition.py derives the reason names from DocumentAssertionRefusalReason and PopulationPlanRefusalReason and asserts the paragraph carries each of them and no other, so the list cannot drift from Core in either direction. Nothing in the adapter changes and no refusal reason is added or removed.
changes.why: At a fixed protocol the five cells of the 2026-09-05 matrix differed in what the producer checked before it stopped, and the adapter's refusal reasons are exactly that list. The Opus and Sonnet producers validated every field against the staged surface and every assertion for a target or a gap unasked; run-17's Haiku producer did neither, and both are rules the skill states without a method. A list the producer can run its own file against is the cheapest thing that carries the rules it already states, and because the list is the adapter's own refusals it steers no modelling decision.
changes.expected_reasons_basis: Core-20 adds no refusal reason and removes none, in either enum. No enum check is possible in either direction, and the entry says so rather than carrying a vacuous subset result. What is readable is the paragraph and the guard.
changes.pin_evidence: The pin reads the skill at the pinned commit, extracts the paragraph between the malleus-preflight-refusals markers, and collects every reason-shaped token in it. LANDED requires the markers present, every reason of both enums named in the paragraph, no token in it that neither enum carries, and tests/test_inquisition.py naming both enum classes and the same marker. Anything less reads PENDING_AT_PIN, and the entry names the reasons that are missing.
changes.pin_evidence_method: The reason list is derived from the two enums at the pinned commit, never typed into this contract, so a Core task that adds a reason after this cell opens makes the paragraph incomplete rather than making the pin silently agree with it.
changes.producer_visible_note: The skill is one of the eight declared inputs, so this change is the one thing in the cell the producer reads. Its bytes are recorded in the producer input manifest at the pinned commit and the workspace is built from those bytes, never from the live tree.
changes.expected_detail: A Haiku 4.5 producer under the v4.10 skill reaches admission within the two structural returns the manifest allows, where run-17 at v4.9 was refused after two. The basis is run-17's own three refusals: all three are on the list, and two of them, the surface validation and the target-or-gap rule, are the two the RCA names as rules the v4.9 skill states without a method.
changes.falsifier_basis: The runner list in this cell's own launch log decides it and no comparison with another cell is needed to read it. A third refusal says a list does not substitute for a producer's own validator, and the paper's claim for small producers stops at the protocol admitting nothing wrong from them.
changes.not_this_cell: Nothing is claimed about any model, and nothing about the list beyond this document and this producer. One cell is one observation. A cell that is admitted will not have shown that the paragraph caused it, only that the outcome the loop predicted from it occurred.

changes.subject: paper-v4/experiment-v4/run-19/native_query.py
changes.detail: native_query.py emits one row per distinct witness per question. A witness is the row's kind and its record ids: record_id for an ENTITY row, record_id and subject_id for a SUBJECT row, relation_id with both endpoint ids for a RELATION row. Two cases that reach one witness produce one row; the row carries case_ordinals, every producing ordinal sorted, in place of case_ordinal, and the rows of a question are ordered by the first ordinal that produced them. The row projects the fields of the witness record's own type as the surface declares them and never the type its case named: for a SUBJECT row each side through its own record's type, for a RELATION row the relation's own type and each endpoint's own type. The per-type projections are read back out of the binding, where the binder already wrote one list per record type off the accepted surface and repeated it in every case naming that type, so bind_from_surface.py does not change and the binding frozen at acceptance with its cases_sha256 stays the executed binding's proof. A type the binding projects two ways, and a record whose own type the binding never names, are both refused rather than guessed past. The subject side still projects tags (E-0156). The result schema moves to malleus.paper-v4.query-result/v3. Nothing else in the executor moves: the three case kinds, the source-free guard, the forbidden-attempt counters and the witness tracer are the bytes every cell from run-02 onward ran, and the producer never sees the file. changes.detail: A third template, instantiated at freeze with the same placeholders as v2. It keeps every duty of run-08's task: the statement read through the retained capture, the statement digest recomputed per located claim, and the derivation-locality token per row. It adds the three row kinds and what each one's witness is, says that a SUBJECT or an ENTITY row is judged on the block the witness's own derivation reaches, and requires a third fixed token on those rows stating whether the subject named in the row occurs in that block: SUBJECT_IN_BLOCK, SUBJECT_NOT_IN_BLOCK or NO_SUBJECT_IN_ROW. RELATION rows carry two tokens and no third. The tokens stay at the head of rationale because the record grammar is closed at four row keys and the validator is frozen. changes.subject: paper-v4/evaluation-v4/review-task-v4.template.md
changes.detail: A fourth template, instantiated at freeze with the same seven placeholders as v3. It keeps every duty of v3: the statement read through the retained capture, the statement digest recomputed per located claim, the three row kinds and what each one's witness is, and the subject-in-block token on SUBJECT and ENTITY rows. One thing moves. The derivation-locality token, DERIVATION_LOCAL or DERIVATION_NON_LOCAL, is written on RELATION rows only. A SUBJECT row already carries the subject token, which is the same statement of fact for that kind of row, and an ENTITY row's locality was local by construction and recorded anyway. On those two kinds the token restated what the row already said. The template states the reason in its own words. The tokens stay at the head of rationale because the record grammar is closed at four row keys and the validator is frozen, and the frozen protocol does not move: this is a task change, not a protocol change. The producer never sees any of it. Carried into v4.7 unchanged: the template is the same file, the seven placeholders are the same, and only the cell it is instantiated to moves.

changes.detail: The research pack's SourceAsserted mixin gains an optional single subject reference, ranged on Entity, to the thing the assertion is about. The document adapter checks it at capture by name: the subject entity's name, whitespace collapsed and case folded, must occur in a statement that formalizes the record, and a SUBJECT_NOT_NAMED refusal names every record that fails, aggregated. Subject coverage joins the census as a reported axis, neither gated nor refused. The pin script fills the pack version and the reason names from the pinned commit, as run-08's pin.py did for Core-12; the baseline is the v4.2 coordinate, so nothing Core-12 landed is counted here. Carried into v4.5 unchanged: this entry states what v4.3 landed, not what v4.5 expects. Its reasons are read between the v4.2 and the v4.3 coordinates, both fixed commits, so a reason Core-15 adds cannot be attributed to Core-13; the pin only records whether SUBJECT_NOT_NAMED is still in force at this coordinate.
changes.why: handover/2026-09-05-v42-rca.md, follow-up 1, approved in E-0139. Run-08's graph held 131 observations and 85 claims and not one relation from any of them to a feature, a sample, a campaign or another claim, while 23 of its 131 observations carried the subject as text inside quantity_kind. The producer's ontology had no predicate for 'this observation is about that thing' and neither did the pack, so the path of least resistance was free text the query surface cannot read. A subject reference at the pack level is connected by definition, checkable, and cheaper than a relation record; an observation with no nameable subject becomes a gap the census counts.

changes.subject: paper-v4/experiment-v4/run-19/native_query.py
changes.detail: native_query.py projects the subject entity's tags beside whatever the binder named for the subject side of a SUBJECT row, wherever the subject record carries the slot. _project already drops a field the record does not have, so a subject with no tags projects exactly what it projected in run-12. The edit is in the executor and not in the binder, because the binder's projection is per record type and its housekeeping set is what the RELATION and ENTITY kinds are projected through too: adding tags there would move every row of every kind and the case bytes with them. Nothing else moves. The case field set is closed at the same keys, output_fields is unchanged, cases_sha256 still digests the queries alone, the binding schema stays malleus.paper-v4.native-query-binding/v4, and the record side of a SUBJECT row, the RELATION rows and the ENTITY rows are byte for byte what run-12's executor returned. The producer never sees the file. run-13's test_pipeline.py states the delta as three exact substitutions and reverses them back to run-12's bytes, so a fourth edit fails the test rather than travelling unnoticed. Carried into v4.9 with the executor it lives in. The subject side still projects tags wherever the subject record carries them; what it projects them beside is now the fields the subject record's own type declares rather than the fields the case named, which is ONE_ROW_PER_WITNESS_OWN_TYPE_PROJECTION's doing and not this entry's. A subject with no tags still projects exactly what it projected before. Carried into run-16 inside an executor that is run-15's byte for byte. Carried into run-17 inside an executor that is run-16's byte for byte. Carried into run-18 inside an executor that is run-17's byte for byte. Carried into run-19 inside an executor that is run-18's byte for byte.
changes.why: Run-11's preliminary review, carried in the overseer journal as the first item of the harness queue after run-12. Nine SUBJECT rows were tokened SUBJECT_NOT_IN_BLOCK because the row showed the entity's name, the full form, where the block wrote the abbreviation one of the entity's tags carries. The check at capture is Core-15's and accepts either form, so the adapter had already agreed the name is in the block; the row was showing the reviewer less than the check had read. Projecting tags beside the name puts the reviewer and the adapter on the same evidence. It is a review-surface change and not a measurement change: no row is added, removed or reordered. The v4.6 RCA states the effect expected of it: the subject-in-block token no longer flagging an abbreviation the entity's tag already carries.

runner_refusals.detail: Fifty defects in one aggregated diagnostic, 9,665 bytes staged in the producer's workspace: 45 SUBJECT_NOT_NAMED, 4 MODALITY_NOT_ASSERTED and 1 EVALUATIVE_SLOT_NOT_EVALUATED. The producer's own validator had checked verbatim statements and formalization targets and none of the three derivation-content rules; it reports extending the validator to all three after the return and finding two more instances. Returned as structural diagnostic 1 of 2.

measured_against.blocks_source: Counted from run-16's frozen capture, the same three labels Core-19's census now writes at admission. Run-16 ran before Core-19, so its own census.json reads 186 blocks REVIEWED and reports no split.
measured_against.anchor_rule: A record counts here when every assertion that formalizes its subject field formalizes no other field of that record.

review.digest_note: No record carries assertion_locator or statement_sha256, so the protocol's one mechanical binding of a claim to its sentence did not run on this cell at all.

measured_against.reason: Run-16 is this cell with one Core coordinate less. Same producer model, same harness, same eight declared inputs but the skill, and the same document; what moves is the skill, which carries Core-20's pre-flight list at the commit this cell pins. Its fifty defects at the first runner attempt are the figure the expectation is stated against, and they are read from its frozen launch log rather than from the ledger.

and_against_the_v4_10_haiku_cell.not_a_control: Run-18 is not this cell's control. It is the same list at the same Core commit read by a different producer, and it ended refused after the diagnostic budget with eleven statements still not verbatim. What it bounds is what the list did not do for a producer that turns no rule into code; it says nothing about what it does for one that does.

secondary_measures.note: Three figures run-16 produced that the protocol reported late or not at all. Core-19 now writes the block split and the provenance coverage at admission, so a cell that repeats any of the three is visible there rather than at review.
